event.summary: Preference test still proves its real backend acknowledgment
event.detail: Reviewed commit: 350a4b33b6d4476f4a78e43cea124bc2b828f462. TLDR: Considered whether replacing browser response body completion with a test gate lets a preference-save test pass without the setting reaching the helm. Source refutes that concern: the owned route awaits route.fetch(), requires status 204 at lines 286-287, and only then releases latestCommitted; the body awaits both the browser response status and that gate before reading preferences at lines 310-318. The test also requires outgoing values [true,false] at line 282, so equal initial and final stored values alone cannot satisfy its action premise. Contract: shared preferences are helm-owned, SPEC.md lines 2357-2364, and test checklist requires an observable distinguishing competing mechanisms. Suggested bucket: other (test evidence only). Confidence: confirmed by source; no execution performed. proposed_drop: source refutation above; this is not a reported defect. could-be-highest: no; no security or user-owned-work-loss route is implicated. possible_cover: none. Caveat: this validates request acknowledgment and persistence, not an independent claim that every later GUI task has retired.
